([[Kansas City, Missouri]]) | college = [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] (2018–2022) | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2022 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2022]]) * [[NCAA Basketball Tournament Most Outstanding Player|NCAA Final Four Most Outstanding Player]] (2022) * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2022]]) * [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] (2022) * First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2022) }} '''Ochai Young Agbaji''' (born April 20, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. As a senior in college, Agbaji was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and voted the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] in 2022. He led the Jayhawks to a national championship and was named the [[NCAA Basketball Tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four Most Outstanding Player]] (MOP). ==Early life== Agbaji was born in [[Milwaukee]], Wisconsin, but grew up in [[Kansas City, Missouri]].{{cite web |last1=Tait |first1=Matt |title=Ochai Agbaji's father, Olofu, explains his son's 'special purpose' after 95–68 Kansas win vs. Milwaukee |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2019/dec/11/ochai-agbajis-father-olofu-explains-his-sons-speci/ |website=KUSports.com |access-date=January 25, 2022 |date=December 11, 2019}} He grew up playing [[association football|soccer]], upon his father's encouragement, playing club soccer as well as [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball from a young age. Agbaji stopped playing soccer as a sophomore at [[Oak Park High School (Kansas City, Missouri)|Oak Park High School]] in [[Kansas City, Missouri]] to focus on basketball. He grew nine inches between his freshman and junior years.{{cite web |last1=Mellinger |first1=Sam |title=How and why Kansas freshman Ochai Agbaji went from overlooked recruit to NBA prospect |url=https://www.kansascity.com/latest-news/article226565829.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |date=February 21, 2019}} In his basketball career at Oak Park, Agbaji did not receive offers from any [[Power Five conferences|Power Five]] college programs until his senior season. As a senior, he averaged 27.6 points and 8.6 rebounds per game for Oak Park and was named ''[[The Kansas City Star|Kansas City Star]]'' All-Metro player of the year.{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |last2=McDowell |first2=Sam |title=It's official: Oak Park senior Ochai Agbaji signs with Kansas basketball |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article208641889.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |date=April 11, 2018}} Agbaji was considered a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite web |last1=Skretta |first1=Dave |title=Jayhawks' Agbaji is proof that big-time talent still sneaks under recruiting radar |url=https://www.foxsports.com/kansas-city/story/kansas-jayhawks-ochai-agbaji-is-proof-that-big-time-talent-still-sneaks-under-recruiting-radar-022519 |website=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |date=February 25, 2019}} On February 8, 2018, he committed to play college basketball for [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] over offers from [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] and [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Ochai Agbaji commits to Kansas |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Ochai-Agbaji-commits-to-Kansas-114883729/ |website=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |date=February 8, 2018}} ==College career== Agbaji started his freshman season at the [[University of Kansas]] as a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] and was a member of the [[Practice squad|scout team]].{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=CJ |title=Redshirt burned, Ochai Agbaji comes up big for Kansas |url=https://theathletic.com/759792/2019/01/10/redshirt-burned-ochai-agbaji-comes-up-big-for-kansas/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |date=January 10, 2019}} In early January 2019, his redshirt was lifted because Kansas needed depth after [[Udoka Azubuike]] suffered a season-ending injury and [[Silvio De Sousa]] faced eligibility issues.{{cite web |last1=Chasen |first1=Scott |title=Ochai Agbaji to burn redshirt, play Bill Self announces |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/Article/Ochai-Agbaji-to-burn-redshirt-play-Bill-Self-announces-on-Hawk-Talk-127548387/ |website=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |date=January 8, 2019}} On January 29, Agbaji made his first career start, scoring 24 points, bringing in seven rebounds, and stealing the ball twice in a loss to [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]]. In his next game, he recorded his first [[double (basketball)|double-double]] in a win over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]]. Agbaji was named [[Big 12 Conference]] Newcomer of the Week for the two performances.{{cite web |title=Agbaji named Big 12 Newcomer of the Week |url=https://kuathletics.com/mens-basketball-agbaji-named-big-12-newcomer-of-the-week/ |publisher=Kansas Jayhawks |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |date=February 4, 2019}} Agbaji averaged 8.5 points and 4.6 rebounds per game in 22 games including 16 starts as a freshman.{{cite news |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title=Agbaji's rapid rise gives KU scoring threat: 'He is poised to have a bust-out year' |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article236894623.html |accessdate=November 23, 2019 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |date=November 1, 2019}} On November 5, 2019, Agbaji made his sophomore season debut scoring 15 points in a loss to fourth-ranked [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] at the [[Champions Classic]].{{cite web |title=No. 3 Kansas upended by No. 4 Duke, 68–66 |url=https://kuathletics.com/gameday-live-champions-classic-vs-duke/ |publisher=Kansas Jayhawks |accessdate=November 19, 2019 |date=November 5, 2019}} During the aforementioned sophomore season, Agbaji was named Honorable Mention All-Big 12.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced |url=https://big12sports.com/documents/2020/3/8//All_Big_12_Release_19_20_.pdf |website=[[Big 12 Conference]] |accessdate=March 8, 2020 |date=March 8, 2020}} As a sophomore, Agbaji averaged 10 points and 4.2 rebounds per game and finished second on the team with 46 three-pointers.{{cite news |last1=Braswell |first1=Scott |title=Azubuike named Big 12 Player of the Year |url=http://www.kten.com/story/41868018/azubuike-named-big-12-player-of-the-year |accessdate=April 4, 2020 |work=KTEN |date=March 8, 2020}} He averaged 14.1 points per game as a junior, shooting 42 percent from the field. On April 8, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Gates |first=Riley |title=Ochai Agbaji declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Kansas-Jayhawks-basketball-Ochai-Agbaji-declares-for-2021-NBA-Draft-Bill-Self-163878833/ |website=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=May 30, 2021 |date=April 8, 2021}} Agbaji made his senior season debut on November 9, 2021, recording 29 points in an 87–74 win against [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] at the Champions Classic.{{cite web |last1=Bedore |first1=Gary |title='He's a pro': Ochai Agbaji scores career-high 29 as KU Jayhawks beat Michigan State |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article255659641.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=November 15, 2021 |date=November 10, 2021}} On January 24, 2022, he scored a career-high 37 points in a 94–91 double overtime win over Texas Tech.{{cite news |title=Agbaji helps No. 5 Kansas beat Texas Tech 94–91 in 2OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401368387 |access-date=January 25, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 25, 2022}} At the close of the season, Agbaji was voted the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] and was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].{{cite press release|url= https://big12sports.com/news/2022/3/6/mens-basketball-all-big-12-awards-announced.aspx |title= Men's Basketball All-Big 12 Awards Announced |publisher=[[Big 12 Conference]] |date=March 6, 2022 |accessdate=March 6, 2022}} Kansas won the [[2022 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2022 NCAA Tournament]], and he scored 12 points in [[2022 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|the championship game]] and was named the [[NCAA Basketball Tournament Most Outstanding Player|tournament MOP]].{{cite news|first=Gary|last=Bedore|title=Kansas Jayhawks' Ochai Agbaji adds NCAA Tournament MOP to All-America, Big 12 awards|date=April 4, 2022|newspaper=The State|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/ncaa/article260105450.html|access-date=April 5, 2022}} On April 24, Agbaji declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |title=Kansas guard Ochai Agbaji declares for 2022 NBA draft, says 'I'll always be a Jayhawk' |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33800854/kansas-guard-ochai-agbaji-declares-2022-nba-draft-says-always-jayhawk ==Personal life== Agbaji's father, Olofu, moved from [[Nigeria]] to the U.S. when he was 17.Keegan, Tom. [http://www2.kusports.com/news/2018/jun/26/tom-keegan-tom-keegan-ochai-agbaji-kus-stealth-rec/ Tom Keegan: Ochai Agbaji, KU’s stealth recruit, fits right in], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]], June 26, 2018.''
